description: Petrol / ethanol blend grades. lhv = lower heating value per litre (drives the fuel model: same energy needed, fewer MJ per litre of ethanol blend). Blend rows are computed from the E0 and E100 rows by volume mixing; the E10 result (31.25 MJ/L) matches AFDC's own published E10 figure, which cross-checks the method.

sources.title: Fuel Properties Comparison (Energy Content, lower heating value)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Alternative Fuels Data Center
sources.note: Gasoline 116,090 Btu/gal (E0), E10 112,114 Btu/gal, ethanol 76,330 Btu/gal. Converted with 1 Btu = 1055.056 J, 1 US gal = 3.785412 L.

sources.title: E20 petrol with RON 95 mandatory from April 1
sources.note: "From April 1, 2026, all petrol pumps across India will sell petrol blended with up to 20 per cent ethanol and a minimum Research Octane Number (RON) of 95."

sources.title: Volume-weighted mixing of E0 and E100 properties
sources.note: x = ethanol volume fraction; property = (1 − x)·E0 + x·E100. LHV: E0 32.356, E100 21.274 MJ/L. Density: E0 0.7475 kg/L (midpoint of the BS-VI 720–775 kg/m3 band), ethanol 0.789 kg/L (anhydrous, 20 °C). Real blends deviate by well under 1 %.

density.note: Midpoint of the 720–775 kg/m3 specification band
